target_customer: B2B companies and finance teams in Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf with overdue invoices
problem: Late customer payments choke cash flow and finance teams chase invoices by hand; Levers automates reminders, reconciliation and collection analytics on top of existing accounting systems.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for accounts receivable automation

founders.name: Ammar Alkhouli
founders.background_notes: YC page: about three years at the fund, an early hire covering strategy, compliance, reporting, marketing and HR.

founders.name: Motasim Zawawi
founders.background_notes: YC page: product manager at Mozn building a SaaS AML and KYC product from scratch. Technical status inferred from engineering degree and product role; treat as moderate confidence.

founders.name: Abdullah Alkharashi
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder by Rasmal and the Daily Dropout newsletter (October 2022) though not on the YC page; no background found.

competitors.name: Tesorio
competitors.what: US accounts receivable and cash flow platform for mid-market B2B companies
competitors.traction_then: Company cited a third straight year of triple-digit revenue growth

competitors.name: Upflow
competitors.funding_then: Series A listed June 2021 by CB Insights, amount undisclosed

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly integrations with accounting and ERP systems plus reminder workflows and reconciliation; routine SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with ERP and data gives some stickiness, but global AR tools were funded and local accounting vendors could add reminders.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wafeq, a regional accounting vendor, partnered with Levers rather than copying it (release undated in sources opened); no acquisition found.

market_need_then: The Gulf B2B market relies on credit terms and slow payment; Levers customers listed on its site are small Saudi firms, and the product was described as extra tooling on existing ERPs. No quantified demand data found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain finance language: unlock trapped cash

brand_strength.rationale: Meaningful word for cash leverage, but generic and shared with other firms; press on the brand itself not found.

pivots.from: Finance as a service: bookkeeping, invoicing and bank reconciliation for startups and SMEs (Rasmal and Daily Dropout descriptions, October 2022)
pivots.to: Focused accounts receivable and collections automation

outcome_analysis: Levers is listed as active with a small team of 8 in Jeddah, partnered with accounting vendor Wafeq, and shows nine named customer logos on its site. The product narrowed from a broad finance outsourcing service to accounts receivable. Funding, revenue and growth are not verified, so the stage of success is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: Bouncewatch lists a $2.0M pre-seed from 2022-09 with Y Combinator, Saudi Technology Ventures and Shorooq Partners; Village.ai lists a seed with Shorooq and Y Combinator without an amount; Latka says self-funded. None recorded as a round. Tesorio's Series B was July 2022, during the batch year. Jawlah article could not be fetched (timeout). Rasmal listed the YC batch as Summer 2021, which is wrong versus the YC page. Completeness pass: the pre-seed rests on Seedtable alone (no amount shown); Bouncewatch separately lists 2.0M dated 2022-09 with Saudi Technology Ventures and Shorooq Partners, not merged because the figures come from different databases.
